A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VeRO research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison; renamed components and relocated material can be matched.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark experiments, cross-model transfer results, and Pawn/Knight optimization studies, including detailed appendix results.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds GEPA comparisons, budget ablations, TerminalBench-2 experiments, and an unrestricted GPQA optimization analysis.

M1.justification: The core abstractions and optimization loop remain unchanged. v4 introduces a Filesystem observation mode that exposes trace and dataset JSON artifacts through the optimizer's working directory alongside the existing viewer-tool interface (Section 4.4), constituting a limited procedural adaptation.

E1.justification: v4 retains the earlier task coverage and adds 89 sandboxed TerminalBench-2 tasks using Terminus-KIRA as the target agent. This materially extends actual evaluation from reasoning, QA, and retail interactions to long-horizon terminal coding (Section 4.4).

E2.justification: Table 2 adds GEPA across all five benchmark tasks while retaining every earlier comparator. This extends comparison beyond coding-agent configurations to an external reflective-evolution optimizer, using Sonnet 4.5 and the same editable components as Resources Only.

E3.justification: New protocols include the five-level budget sweep, TerminalBench-2 optimization and evaluation on the same 89 tasks with sample budgets of 89/178 and pass/error metrics, and unrestricted GPQA evaluation with post-hoc judging. v4 also corrects the blanket validation-based checkpoint-selection statement to training-based selection for GPQA; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v4 adds budget sensitivity analysis across all five benchmark tasks (Figure 8), TerminalBench-2 error-category and task-level gain/regression analyses (Appendix A.4), and an unrestricted GPQA study examining test-data exposure and budget violations (Appendix A.5). Earlier transfer, instruction, and trajectory analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v4 newly specifies deterministic seeded splits and distinguishes optimizer variability from unmeasured evaluation stochasticity. Figure 8 explicitly labels uncertainty as one standard deviation across three runs, and TerminalBench-2 configurations are identified as single-run results. The earlier benchmark and Pawn/Knight repetition counts remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Retained Table 2 rows, Table 3 transfer scores, and Pawn/Knight appendix results are numerically unchanged. Added results include GEPA's 0.54 average, budget-dependent outcomes, and TerminalBench-2 pass counts of 30/89, 27/89, and 33/89 across the three new configurations against a 27/89 baseline. Appendix A.5 additionally reports observed leakage and budget overruns.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 retains the formal task definition, restricted program space, budget-constrained objective, lift expression, and optimizer-update equation. No substantive mathematical derivation, theorem, assumption, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The principal harness, benchmark, and empirical contributions remain. v4 extends the claimed benchmark scope to long-horizon coding, emphasizes contamination and budget violations when motivating infrastructure, and adds the conclusion that reasoning-task headroom appears bounded by the target model.

C2.justification: v4 interprets GEPA/Resources Only similarity as support for broader harness changes and flat reasoning-task budget curves as evidence of model-limited headroom. It adds explanations of failure-mode migration and offsetting regressions, explicitly limits interface conclusions because of single runs, and replaces the unexplored budget-sensitivity limitation with unexplored budget allocation.

D1.justification: v4 substantially expands reproducibility information: dataset filtering and split construction in Appendix A.2.1, optimizer turn limits, TerminalBench-2 costs, timing, tokens and code-change details, and verbatim unrestricted-experiment prompts, judging rubric, and trace excerpts. The existing VeRO code-access information is retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds references to GEPA, GPTSwarm, Terminus-KIRA, and Meta-Harness. A new concurrent-work paragraph acknowledges that Meta-Harness addresses the same problem and distinguishes VeRO through optimization guardrails; most earlier related-work discussion remains.

P1.justification: v4 updates the title, author-name presentation, and terminology, distinguishing the outer harness, VeRO-Agent, and VeRO-Bench. The abstract and selected paragraphs are rewritten and appendix subsections are expanded, while most existing prose and the main section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column branded layout to a two-column conference format, with substantial resizing and relocation of displays. Earlier plotted figures are retained, while v4 adds budget plots, transition heatmaps, TerminalBench-2 tables, and prompt/trace listings; Table 2 gains a GEPA row.

improvement.justification: v4 addresses important evidential gaps through the budget sweep, external GEPA comparison, and documented failures without enforced guardrails. Dataset-construction disclosures and detailed regression analyses also substantially improve auditability. TerminalBench-2 remains an in-sample, single-run study, and the budget sweep alone does not prove a target-model ceiling, but these limits do not outweigh the stronger empirical support and reproducibility information.
